statusDetail: Coverage-complete audit of the redirected canonical site https://isaidub.ceo/ across home, listing, detail, download-step, updates, and error paths.

page.notes: https://isaidub.guru redirects to https://isaidub.ceo/. Public Tamil-dubbed movie catalog. Representative templates audited; year variants and other movie details were deduplicated as shared templates. Checkout/account/forms were not covered because none exist.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated dark preference, screenshot, and computed-style/CSS probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the body remained rgb(249,249,249) with black text and computed color-scheme was normal; the dark screenshot matched the light rendering.

checkOutcomes.method: Emulated reduced-motion condition and getAnimations() probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, document.getAnimations() returned an empty list on the home template, so no active non-essential motion remained to suppress.

checkOutcomes.method: Forced-colors screenshot and computed-color probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under forced-colors: active, body colors mapped to black/white system colors and links to yellow; text and links remained visible.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative route walkthrough plus CSS feature probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The MPA has meaningful home, listing, detail, and download-step navigations, but DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition CSS or opt-in; route changes are abrupt full-document swaps.

checkOutcomes.method: Screenshot, DOM, CSS, and animation feature inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No parallax, scrollytelling, entry/exit reveal, carousel, or other scroll-linked motion exists on the sampled templates, so there is no scroll-linked effect to implement declaratively.
checkOutcomes.reason: No scroll-linked motion is present on the representative templates.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM control inventory and representative path walkthrough.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The site exposes ordinary links and pagination only; no swipe, drag, pull-to-refresh, carousel, or custom pointer gesture was present on sampled paths.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile layout measurement and CSS feature inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The recent-updates template is 57,034 CSS pixels tall, but CSS/DOM inspection found no sticky progress, shrinking header, or scroll-state affordance.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM overlay inventory and screenshots.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No tooltip, popover, menu, or other anchored overlay appears on the sampled templates (zero dialog/popover elements).
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no anchored overlay to position.

checkOutcomes.method: Heading/landmark probe and mobile screenshots.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Detail and updates templates have no h1 and no breadcrumb or main/nav landmarks; the 57,034px updates stream offers no location/progress cue beyond date text.

checkOutcomes.method: First-load screenshots and DOM overlay inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Load screenshots across four templates show content immediately with no full-viewport popup, consent wall, interstitial, or overlay; DOM reports no dialog/popover.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM inventory for dialog, popover, details, forms, and overlays.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No transient disclosure, modal flow, select, or overlay exists on the sampled paths, so no dismissible custom primitive needs evaluation.
checkOutcomes.reason: No overlay or disclosure control exists.

checkOutcomes.method: Full-page screenshots, body-text recon, and layout height.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The home page repeats keyword-heavy promotional copy and 21 near-identical update rows before its category navigation; the updates page is a 57,034px undifferentiated stream.

checkOutcomes.method: Mobile layout primitive on four templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: At 360x800, all four templates reported scrollWidth 360, clientWidth 360, viewport meta present, and 0px horizontal overflow.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered CSS feature probe across reusable components.
checkOutcomes.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container or container-type rules; reusable movie, folder, pagination, and form components adapt only through viewport media queries.

checkOutcomes.method: Programmatic focus and bounding-box inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Keyboard focus is visible, but many category links measure only 14px high and update links 17px high, well below a comfortable touch target.

checkOutcomes.method: First-viewport screenshots, headings, and body-text walkthrough.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The home h1 and introductory text identify the Tamil-dubbed catalog, listing titles name their year, and detail content presents movie facts; the next content links are visible in each first viewport.

checkOutcomes.method: Four-step route walkthrough with DOM and screenshots.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The representative journey completed predictably from a home Download Now link to movie detail, then Red Eye (Original), then explicit 720p/360p choices with real hrefs and no account wall.

checkOutcomes.method: Intentional missing-route navigation, screenshot, and DOM probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A missing URL returns a bare Apache 404 with no site chrome, home link, search, retry, or recovery action.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse mobile audit corroborated by trace and layout observers.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 4.2s (poor), despite CLS 0 and TBT 0ms; the separate desktop trace measured LCP about 1.0s, so the mobile load remains the failing common condition.

checkOutcomes.method: Layout-shift observers and Lighthouse.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Layout observers measured CLS 0 to 0.000103 across all four templates, and Lighthouse measured CLS 0.

checkOutcomes.method: Trace summary, long-task observers, and Lighthouse.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The trace and all layout captures recorded no long tasks and 0ms total blocking time; Lighthouse also measured TBT 0ms.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR initiator/priority review confirmed against DOM script async attributes, response headers, and Lighthouse.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The HAR confirms two parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets (site CSS plus Google Fonts), while the document is cache-control:no-store and mobile LCP is 4.2s; the async scripts are not counted as render-blocking.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse unused-code audit and HAR byte attribution.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 67 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR shows Google Tag Manager alone transfers 152,705 bytes versus 15,701 first-party bytes.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM semantic inventory, image primitive, and Lighthouse accessibility audits.
checkOutcomes.evidence: All 17 home images have alt text, links use native anchors, and no form controls or canvas are present; Lighthouse image-alt passed.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse computed contrast audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found repeated red 14px rating text at 3.79:1 and the white Page Keywords label on #36a8da at 2.7:1, below the required 4.5:1.

checkOutcomes.method: Focus walk plus heading/landmark DOM inventory on representative templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Focus is visible, but only a header landmark exists on home and the detail/updates templates contain no headings; there are no main, nav, or footer landmarks.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed CSS, mobile screenshots, and layout height.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Body text is fixed at 14px and the updates page renders a 57,034px dense stream with long link labels and little grouping; screenshots show cramped scanability on mobile.

checkOutcomes.method: Viewport/reflow layout and element bounding-box probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Reflow has no horizontal overflow and user scaling is allowed, but many links have only 14px to 17px high hit areas, failing comfortable touch-target sizing.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse Runtime/console audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reported no browser errors logged to the console.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM document probe and image inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but all sampled folder images omit authored width/height attributes; the detail poster also omits dimensions.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse BFCache and inspector-issues audits.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons due cache-control:no-store/cookie modification and DevTools Issues entries from the ad-tech request chain.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM metadata probes and discoverability fetch comparison.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Home, listing, detail, and updates templates each expose a descriptive title and meta description; raw no-JS HTML preserves them.

checkOutcomes.method: Anchor inventory, mobile layout, and robots inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Content links use real hrefs and the viewport is mobile-friendly, but footer Contact Us and DMCA links both point to the homepage, and the home page repeats generic “Download Now” link text for many different destinations.

checkOutcomes.method: Head metadata probes, response fetches, robots.txt, and sitemap request.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Public pages return 200 and robots allows search indexing, but no canonical or hreflang appears on sampled templates and /sitemap.xml returns an Apache 404 page.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM query for JSON-LD and social metadata on detail/listing templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The movie detail is a rich entity but exposes no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter Card metadata on the visible movie page.

checkOutcomes.method: Security headers and cookie primitives plus HTTPS response inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent; PHPSESSID is neither Secure nor HttpOnly and has SameSite=None.

checkOutcomes.method: Trackers, HAR byte attribution, and cookie audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The page contacts five third-party origins, including Google Analytics and an ad-tech script; third parties account for 178,172 of 193,873 transferred bytes and analytics cookies live 400 days.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative flow inventory and permission/auth API DOM probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No sign-in/account flow exists and no geolocation, notification, camera, microphone, or other permission prompt fired on load.
checkOutcomes.reason: The public download catalog has no authentication or permission-requesting feature.

checkOutcomes.method: Headers and cookie primitives.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors is configured, and cookies use a weak SameSite=None posture.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability raw-fetch versus rendered-DOM comparison and crawler screenshot pair.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Raw server HTML contains 100% of rendered content words on both home and detail, with title/description intact and no empty JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Path walkthrough, DOM inventory, layouts, and Lighthouse console audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The sampled site is server-rendered with ordinary links, no overlays or fragile async UI, no horizontal overflow, and no console errors during representative navigation.

checkOutcomes.method: Manifest/service-worker capability probe and site-type judgement.
checkOutcomes.evidence: This is a public content/download catalog rather than an app-like installed experience; no manifest exists, so offline/installability is not a proportionate requirement for this check.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site is a conventional content catalog, not an app-like surface requiring installation.

checkOutcomes.method: Intentional missing-route screenshot and DOM probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The tested 404 is a bare server page with no branded context, home link, search, retry, or useful recovery path.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM lang attribute plus rendered CSS inspection.
checkOutcomes.evidence: html lang=en matches most sampled prose, but CSS uses physical padding-left, margin-right, and border-left in reusable components and has no dir strategy, so the layout is not translation/bidi ready for its Tamil-language audience.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered content and DOM/source-level script inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The public catalog renders fixed editorial dates and numeric ratings but has no user locale selector, currency, input, or dynamic locale-sensitive calculation to exercise.
checkOutcomes.reason: No dynamic locale-sensitive data feature is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Rendered content and script/API inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No event scheduling, user-entered time, recurring interval, or cross-zone time calculation exists on the sampled catalog pages.
checkOutcomes.reason: The site has no time-zone-sensitive feature.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual inspection and primary journey walkthrough.
checkOutcomes.evidence: First-load and download-journey screenshots show no consent wall, confirmshaming, forced continuity, disguised control, or cancellation flow; links behave predictably.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM form/control inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No user-submittable form or editable field exists on the representative public templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: There is no form validation flow to evaluate.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM form and input inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No address, payment, sign-in, sign-up, search, or other input field appears on the sampled templates.
checkOutcomes.reason: There are no user input fields requiring autofill assistance.

checkOutcomes.method: Representative route and control inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No checkout, subscription, consent, authentication, or account-management surface appears in the representative journey.
checkOutcomes.reason: No commercial or account flow exists in the sampled scope.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR resource-type/weight summary and image-format inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The home transfers only 4,336 image bytes; repeated folder art is one cached 713-byte SVG and no legacy raster formats appear there.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR attribution and Lighthouse unused-JS audit.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A simple static catalog transfers 178,172 third-party bytes, mainly analytics/ad scripts, versus 15,701 first-party bytes; Lighthouse estimates 67 KiB of JavaScript is unused.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR and tracker primitives.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Third parties consume about 92% of transferred bytes, with Google Tag Manager at 152,705 bytes and additional analytics/ad origins despite no rich media requirement.

checkOutcomes.method: Discoverability and feature inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The site is a read-only crawlable content catalog with no transactional or productivity capability that needs WebMCP tool registration; raw content is already fully machine-readable.
checkOutcomes.reason: No agent-action surface exists; ordinary crawlable content is the appropriate interface.

checkOutcomes.method: Feature and script/API inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: No summarisation, generation, translation workflow, or other inference feature is offered where on-device AI would improve the experience.

checkOutcomes.method: Interaction inventory across representative paths.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The server-rendered site has ordinary document navigations and no modal, SPA route, editor, infinite scroll, or other same-document interaction to repeat about ten times without fabricating a test.
checkOutcomes.reason: No representative repeated same-document interaction exists.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary plus performance.memory and DOM-node count.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A settled home state used about 3.51 MB JS heap with 220 DOM elements; the heap summary reports 3.56 MB total self size, proportionate for the page.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap constructor summary and interaction/DOM inventory.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The single-state heap summary shows no Detached* constructor among the reported populations, and the static page has no repeated same-document lifecycle that accumulates listeners or timers.

principleOutcomes.reason: All checks were judged not applicable to this site type.

paths.description: Entry page and category hub; covers first impression, global chrome, metadata, preferences, performance, privacy, and navigation.
2026 year listing; representative of year/category archive templates and pagination.
Red Eye movie detail; representative rich entity/detail and first step of primary download journey.
Red Eye quality-selection step; verifies the primary journey exposes concrete 720p/360p choices.
Recent updates archive; highest-risk long-content/listing template.
Intentional missing route; tests HTTP failure and recovery state.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the body remained rgb(249,249,249) with black text and computed color-scheme was normal; the dark screenshot matched the light rendering.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and retint surfaces/text with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: The MPA has meaningful home, listing, detail, and download-step navigations, but DOM/CSS inspection found no view-transition CSS or opt-in; route changes are abrupt full-document swaps.
findings.suggestedFix: Opt eligible MPA pages into same-origin cross-document View Transitions, with a reduced-motion override.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: The recent-updates template is 57,034 CSS pixels tall, but CSS/DOM inspection found no sticky progress, shrinking header, or scroll-state affordance.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lightweight sticky section/progress affordance for the very long updates archive.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page jumps guide attention (highlight effects, scroll/carousel markers, directional transitions, drill-down and drawer navigation) so the user can follow where focus moved.
findings.evidence: Detail and updates templates have no h1 and no breadcrumb or main/nav landmarks; the 57,034px updates stream offers no location/progress cue beyond date text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add semantic main/nav/footer landmarks, page h1 headings, breadcrumbs, and current-location cues.

findings.summary: Minimise non-content chrome and borders so the content is the focus, not the application frame; expressive/decorative visuals serve the content rather than crowd it.
findings.evidence: The home page repeats keyword-heavy promotional copy and 21 near-identical update rows before its category navigation; the updates page is a 57,034px undifferentiated stream.
findings.suggestedFix: Move keyword copy out of the primary scan path, deduplicate updates, and introduce concise grouping/filtering.

findings.summary: Components adapt to their container with container queries (incl. anchored container queries) and content/state-based styling where reused at different sizes, not only global viewport breakpoints.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no @container or container-type rules; reusable movie, folder, pagination, and form components adapt only through viewport media queries.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards/lists container contexts and adapt their internal layout with @container where reuse warrants it.

findings.summary: Touch targets are adequately sized and hover-only affordances have a non-hover fallback, and keyboard focus is visible, so the UI works for touch, pointer and keyboard alike.
findings.evidence: Keyboard focus is visible, but many category links measure only 14px high and update links 17px high, well below a comfortable touch target.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase interactive hit areas to at least roughly 44 CSS pixels without shrinking visible focus styles.

findings.summary: Loading, empty, success, error, offline, and partial-completion states are visible and actionable; users can retry, undo, cancel, go back, or continue without losing context.
findings.evidence: A missing URL returns a bare Apache 404 with no site chrome, home link, search, retry, or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve a branded 404 with a concise explanation, home/search links, and recovery actions.

findings.summary: Core Web Vitals are in the good range: LCP is fast, interaction latency (INP) is low, and CLS is minimal; work is prioritised and deferred sensibly.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 4.2s (poor), despite CLS 0 and TBT 0ms; the separate desktop trace measured LCP about 1.0s, so the mobile load remains the failing common condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile mobile LCP, shorten the font/style critical path, and remove nonessential load work.

findings.summary: Critical resources are delivered efficiently: cache headers are useful, render-blocking chains are short, fonts do not block or shift text, HTTP delivery is modern, and network dependency trees do not delay the main content.
findings.evidence: The HAR confirms two parser-inserted high-priority stylesheets (site CSS plus Google Fonts), while the document is cache-control:no-store and mobile LCP is 4.2s; the async scripts are not counted as render-blocking.
findings.suggestedFix: Cache public HTML appropriately, self-host/subset or system-fallback fonts, and keep only truly critical CSS in the initial chain.

findings.summary: The page does not ship large unused or duplicated JavaScript/CSS, avoidable legacy bundles, or third-party code that dominates the load without user value.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 67 KiB unused JavaScript; HAR shows Google Tag Manager alone transfers 152,705 bytes versus 15,701 first-party bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or delay analytics/ad JavaScript until it provides explicit user value/consent.

findings.summary: Text and essential UI meet WCAG colour-contrast minimums against their background.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found repeated red 14px rating text at 3.79:1 and the white Page Keywords label on #36a8da at 2.7:1, below the required 4.5:1.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the red and cyan combinations with tokens that meet WCAG contrast at 14px.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is logical, focus order follows reading order, keyboard focus is always visible, and interactive state survives DOM moves.
findings.evidence: Focus is visible, but only a header landmark exists on home and the detail/updates templates contain no headings; there are no main, nav, or footer landmarks.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap content in main, navigation in nav, footer links in footer, and add one meaningful h1 per template.

findings.summary: Text is legible and inclusively rendered: comfortable line layout, precise alignment, stable rendering across mixed fonts, no clipping or cramped wrapping that harms comprehension.
findings.evidence: Body text is fixed at 14px and the updates page renders a 57,034px dense stream with long link labels and little grouping; screenshots show cramped scanability on mobile.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase base size/line spacing and group the updates archive into scannable dated sections or pagination.

findings.summary: The experience remains usable when zoomed or reflowed, touch targets are large enough, media has captions or equivalents where needed, and the viewport does not prevent user scaling.
findings.evidence: Reflow has no horizontal overflow and user scaling is allowed, but many links have only 14px to 17px high hit areas, failing comfortable touch-target sizing.
findings.suggestedFix: Expand link hit areas with block/flex padding while retaining fluid reflow.

findings.summary: Valid doctype and charset, images sized with correct aspect ratio, no deprecated APIs misused, and CSS/HTML are well structured and not needlessly repetitive. (HTTPS, CSP and permission hygiene are judged under be-private-and-secure, not here.)
findings.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but all sampled folder images omit authored width/height attributes; the detail poster also omits dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Author intrinsic width and height on images/posters to reserve aspect-ratio space.

findings.summary: The page uses the platform cleanly: no deprecated APIs, no avoidable BFCache blockers, no broken source maps or inspector issues, no stale vulnerable libraries, no paste-prevention on inputs, and no notification/geolocation prompts on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports three BFCache failure reasons due cache-control:no-store/cookie modification and DevTools Issues entries from the ad-tech request chain.
findings.suggestedFix: Stop marking public pages no-store where unnecessary and remove the ad-tech chain causing DevTools issues.

findings.summary: Links are crawlable (real href), there is a viewport meta tag, robots does not block indexing, and link text is descriptive.
findings.evidence: Content links use real hrefs and the viewport is mobile-friendly, but footer Contact Us and DMCA links both point to the homepage, and the home page repeats generic “Download Now” link text for many different destinations.
findings.suggestedFix: Give Contact/DMCA their real URLs and make repeated link text identify the destination.

findings.summary: Public pages expose the indexing signals search engines need: successful HTTP status, canonical URL when appropriate, hreflang for localized variants, robots/sitemap consistency, and no accidental noindex/noarchive policy.
findings.evidence: Public pages return 200 and robots allows search indexing, but no canonical or hreflang appears on sampled templates and /sitemap.xml returns an Apache 404 page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referencing canonicals and publish a valid sitemap referenced by robots.txt.

findings.summary: Where the page represents an article, product, organization, event, place or other rich entity, structured data and share-preview metadata accurately describe the visible content.
findings.evidence: The movie detail is a rich entity but exposes no JSON-LD, Open Graph, or Twitter Card metadata on the visible movie page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Movie JSON-LD and Open Graph/Twitter metadata matching visible detail content.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, framing protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent; PHPSESSID is neither Secure nor HttpOnly and has SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking, referrer and permissions policies; set PHPSESSID Secure, HttpOnly and Lax/Strict.

findings.summary: No over-collection of user data, no leaky third parties, and analytics/background data collection is minimised and batched rather than chatty or session-wide by default.
findings.evidence: The page contacts five third-party origins, including Google Analytics and an ad-tech script; third parties account for 178,172 of 193,873 transferred bytes and analytics cookies live 400 days.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the opaque ad origin and minimise or consent-gate analytics with a short retention period.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are configured where appropriate: HSTS, clickjacking protection (frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options), Trusted Types for XSS-sensitive apps, origin isolation, privacy-preserving third-party cookie posture, and sensible Referrer-Policy / Permissions-Policy.
findings.evidence: No HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, or CSP frame-ancestors is configured, and cookies use a weak SameSite=None posture.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy browser-enforced CSP/frame-ancestors, HSTS, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: HTTP errors, network failures, timeouts and stale data states are handled intentionally: users see useful recovery options rather than blank screens, infinite spinners, broken shells, or misleading success states.
findings.evidence: The tested 404 is a bare server page with no branded context, home link, search, retry, or useful recovery path.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the server-default 404 with an intentional, navigable recovery page.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: html lang=en matches most sampled prose, but CSS uses physical padding-left, margin-right, and border-left in reusable components and has no dir strategy, so the layout is not translation/bidi ready for its Tamil-language audience.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace physical left/right spacing and borders with logical inline/block properties and test dir=rtl.

findings.summary: Background work and fetching are not wasteful: background processing is efficient and de-prioritised, and the lightest technique that achieves the result is preferred over heavy or redundant work.
findings.evidence: A simple static catalog transfers 178,172 third-party bytes, mainly analytics/ad scripts, versus 15,701 first-party bytes; Lighthouse estimates 67 KiB of JavaScript is unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate analytics/ad work that outweighs the first-party page and defer any retained telemetry.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts, fonts, video, audio, animation and heavy media are proportionate to the user value they provide; autoplay or background media is avoided unless essential and resource use is cached or deferred where possible.
findings.evidence: Third parties consume about 92% of transferred bytes, with Google Tag Manager at 152,705 bytes and additional analytics/ad origins despite no rich media requirement.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a strict third-party byte budget and remove the 153 KB tag manager/ad chain from initial load.
